sources.title: Dead Cells — Thomas Vasseur, Art Design Deep Dive (2018)
sources.read_extent: Developer article; key-frame and rendering sections
sources.evidence: Convincing timing and minimal keys precede extra drawings; attacks are pose-to-pose. The reported character height is 50 pixels.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer pose economy and retiming to our fixed controller. Exclude the 3D renderer, interpolation, normal maps and blended VFX.

sources.title: Katana ZERO — Justin Stander interview (2019)
sources.read_extent: Firsthand developer answers; controls/design passages
sources.evidence: Stander describes controls as an extension of the player's intended action, with considerable attention to small details.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer input-to-action clarity. This interview supplies no verified attack exposures or smear counts.

sources.title: Hollow Knight — Ari Gibson and William Pellen (2018 interview, published 2025)
sources.read_extent: Firsthand transcript; terrain/movement discussion
sources.evidence: The directors connect snappy movement and straight terrain with judging distances and behavior.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer spatial honesty. NEVERLOOKBACK already has acceleration; do not replace it with Hollow Knight's movement model.

sources.title: Hyper Light Drifter — Alx Preston and Teddy Dief (2013)
sources.read_extent: Firsthand developer interview; combat/art sections
sources.evidence: They describe art and movement reinforcing a nimble, adept fighter and a world communicated visually.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer agreement between characterization and motion. Our civilian must convey a different capability. This is pre-release testimony, not final frame-timing evidence.

sources.title: My Friend Pedro — Victor Ågren (2019)
sources.read_extent: Firsthand developer interview; animation/control and contrast passages
sources.evidence: Ågren prioritizes players controlling the character over watching locked animation; describes dynamic blending and contrast against environments.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer interruptible presentation and background checks. Exclude procedural bones, blending and acrobatic gunfighter poses.

sources.title: Mark of the Ninja — Nels Anderson and Jamie Cheng postmortem (2013; reprint 2017)
sources.read_extent: Developer-written postmortem; readability/playtesting passages
sources.evidence: Animation cues and visual communication were developed around players understanding actions in a dark environment; playtesting exposed communication issues.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer unfamiliar-viewer state identification. Do not borrow ninja stance, stealth systems or heroic silhouette.

sources.title: Blasphemous — The Game Kitchen, How characters are created (2017)
sources.read_extent: Official creator update; named character-creation section
sources.evidence: Mechanic/context definition precedes silhouette exploration, a standing sprite tested against real scenes, expressive drafts and handcrafted animation.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer staged rejection and contextual readability. Exclude borrowed placeholders, concept downsampling, Unity plugins and gameplay retuning.

sources.title: SANABI — Wonder Potion interview (2023)
sources.read_extent: Firsthand developer answers; control, feedback and art sections
sources.evidence: The team identifies control feel as central to its constantly used chain mechanic and describes studying player footage to locate frustration.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer a visible causal relationship to actual mechanics. Do not add chain motion, assistance, superhero capability or their sketch-conversion pipeline.

sources.title: Stan Prokopenko — How to Draw Gesture
sources.read_extent: Instructor lesson notes; not community comments
sources.evidence: Gesture connects masses and expresses an action rather than tracing contours; broad action rhythms and contrasting axes organize the figure.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer a whole-body intention before cuffs, folds or flame. Line of action is a drawing abstraction, not a measured center of mass.

sources.title: Stan Prokopenko — Structure in the Body: Robo Bean
sources.read_extent: Instructor lesson notes, landmarks/motion/twist
sources.evidence: Separate ribcage and pelvis volumes clarify tilt, lean, twisting and overlapping planes.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer connected torso masses and consistent foreshortening. Boxes are analytical scaffolding, never procedural production body parts.

sources.title: Shawn Kelly — Twinning (2017)
sources.read_extent: Animator-authored article; posing and timing sections
sources.evidence: Matching poses and timing across paired parts can remove contrast and overlap; deliberate symmetry can still communicate an intended action.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer motivated unequal limbs. Do not add random asymmetry or prohibit a brief bilateral protective response.

sources.title: Nathaniel Seymour / Animation Mentor — Overlap and Follow-Through (2025)
sources.read_extent: Written tutorial summary and tips; embedded video not watched
sources.evidence: Primary action leads; attached parts trail and settle. Excess overlap floats; negative space must remain clear.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer body-first secondary flame and material response. Exclude Maya controls, graph-editor smoothing and automatic offsets.

sources.title: Kevin Koch — Slow In and Slow Out (2017)
sources.read_extent: Animator-authored article; spacing and alternative stop solutions
sources.evidence: Timing and spacing differ. Different parts follow their own paths; abrupt stops, recoil and overshoot can be appropriate alternatives to smooth easing.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer deliberate spacing inside existing durations. Do not tween raster frames or impose cinematic slowdowns.

sources.title: Pedro Medeiros — Thoughts on Low Resolution (2022)
sources.read_extent: Artist's complete article text and examples
sources.evidence: Meaning comes from selective pixels, meaningful colors and readable masses; details and texture need a reason.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer omission and material hierarchy. A successful small example is not evidence that this protagonist already reads at 1×.

sources.title: Pedro Medeiros — Pixel Art Glossary
sources.read_extent: Artist's complete glossary text
sources.evidence: Connected same-color pixels form clusters; isolated pixels attract attention, and diagonal connections are weaker than full side connections.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer cluster inspection and justified exceptions. Connectivity statistics cannot prove anatomy or character identity.

sources.title: cure — The Pixel Art Tutorial (2010, edited 2014)
sources.read_extent: Original artist tutorial; clusters, banding, shading, noise and value sections
sources.evidence: Adjacent clusters shape each other; banding, pillow shading and unnecessary independent pixels can obscure form.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer precise neighboring shapes and directional value masses. The tutorial's general AA/dithering advice does not override this project's exclusions.

sources.title: Stan Prokopenko — How to Draw Interesting Shapes
sources.read_extent: Instructor's public written summary only; video not watched
sources.evidence: The summary identifies variety, contrast, complexity, symmetry, tension, balance, shifted peaks and tilted axes as shape-design tools.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer uneven shape hierarchy. Do not attribute detailed procedures or AI-provenance claims to this short summary.

sources.title: Lu et al. — Anticipatory postural adjustments during gait initiation (2017)
sources.read_extent: Original paper; indexed abstract, introduction/discussion excerpts; direct page challenged access
sources.evidence: Self-paced initiation in 157 ambulatory adults showed substantial variability in anticipatory components, including absent components.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer purposeful load transfer without a mandatory universal start sequence. Center of pressure is not center of mass; no lab latency becomes a game delay.

sources.title: Sanders et al. — Protective balance and startle responses to sudden freefall (2015)
sources.read_extent: Original paper; indexed methods/discussion/conclusion excerpts; direct page challenged access
sources.evidence: Nine healthy participants experienced externally triggered versus self-triggered platform drops; first reactions included pronounced neck/arm activity and arm abduction, with habituation.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer a plausible unexpected flinch contrasted with intended action. This is not evidence for a universal fighting stance or for every reaction being protective.

sources.title: Arellano and Kram — Is swinging the arms worth it? (2014)
sources.read_extent: Original paper; abstract, methods and rotation/discussion excerpts
sources.evidence: Restricting arm swing in runners increased shoulder and pelvis rotation; arm swing helps counter rotational effects of leg motion.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer coupled arm/torso behavior. Distance runners at a laboratory pace do not establish a civilian's panic-running style.

sources.title: Solis-Escalante et al. — Balance perturbations and reactive stepping (2021)
sources.read_extent: Original paper; abstract, participant/task and discussion excerpts
sources.evidence: Eleven young able-bodied participants recovered from translated support surfaces with feet-in-place or stepping responses; responses varied with disturbance.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer visible support restoration after overreach. Do not transplant EEG results, laboratory delays or a physical step into gameplay.

sources.title: Pedro Medeiros — Motion Blur tutorial
sources.read_extent: Original 512×512 tutorial; locally inspected frames 0, 16, 31 of 32
sources.evidence: The illustrated lesson connects a motion smear to the preceding position and uses it to clarify complex movement.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer a source/path/destination requirement. Exclude complementary-color flashes, ghost skulls, detached trails and magical arcs.

sources.title: Pedro Medeiros — Run Cycle 1 tutorial
sources.read_extent: Original 512×512 tutorial; locally inspected frames 0, 16, 31 of 32
sources.evidence: The lesson distinguishes airborne/high, descent, contact and low/recovery phases and demonstrates an opposite-leg half.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer complete support alternation. Do not copy its pose silhouettes, repeat a mirrored half, or mandate its example drawing counts.

sources.title: Pedro Medeiros — Attack Animation tutorial
sources.read_extent: Original 512×512 tutorial; locally inspected frames 0, 18, 35 of 36
sources.evidence: The example emphasizes timing and return, with a warning that a long player anticipation can feel like lag.
sources.transfer_boundary: Transfer distinct action/return within the audited clock. NEVERLOOKBACK already has 50 ms startup; retain it. Exclude example count and sword poses.
